candidates.name: Drug-induced liver injury
support_spans: On day 9 of therapy, he reported loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice.
He was started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily.
candidates.why: The patient developed liver injury after starting Alfuzosin, suggesting a potential drug-induced cause.

candidates.name: Acute viral hepatitis
contradict_spans: Serologic tests for HBsAg, anti-HBc IgM, anti-HCV, anti-HAV IgM, anti-HEV, HEV RNA, and HCV RNA were negative.
candidates.why: The patient presented with jaundice and elevated liver enzymes, but negative serologic tests make this diagnosis less likely.

candidates.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
contradict_spans: Autoimmune markers (ANA, AMA, ASMA, LKM-1) were negative.
candidates.why: The patient's liver enzyme elevation could suggest autoimmune hepatitis, but negative autoimmune markers make this diagnosis less likely.

candidates.name: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) due to Alfuzosin
support_spans: On day 9 of therapy, he reported loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice
contradict_spans: He denied use of aspirin, acetaminophen, or herbal medicines and had no history of liver disease
candidates.why: The patient developed liver injury after starting Alfuzosin, suggesting a possible drug-induced cause
candidates.protected_reason: DILI is a rare but potentially severe side effect of certain medications, and Alfuzosin is not commonly associated with liver injury, making it a minority consideration

candidates.name: Acute viral hepatitis due to an uncommon virus

contradict_spans: He denied use of aspirin, acetaminophen, or herbal medicines and had no history of liver disease

candidates.name: Idiopathic acute cholestasis
support_spans: Abdominal ultrasonography showed normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts
contradict_spans: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography demonstrated a normal biliary anatomy
candidates.why: The patient's normal imaging studies and lack of obvious bile duct obstruction suggest a possible idiopathic cause for his cholestasis
candidates.protected_reason: Idiopathic acute cholestasis is a rare condition that may not have a clear underlying cause, making it a minority consideration
